A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CoIRL-AD. All 18 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original nuScenes and Navsim experiments, ablations, cross-city and long-tail evaluations, training diagnostics and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 reports original nuScenes experiments, including retained benchmark results, expanded ablations, reconstructed long-tail evaluations and new RL comparisons.

M1.justification: The core procedure remains unchanged: backward-masked Gaussian waypoint policies, step-aware group sampling, imagined-state actor–critic learning, behavior-cloning regularization and competitive parameter transfer. Equations 1–17 and Algorithm 1 retain these components; additional hyperparameters and explanations document the existing method.

E1.justification: v2 removes the entire Navsim evaluation reported in v1 Sections 4.1–4.3 and Table 2, substantially narrowing dataset coverage. nuScenes, Singapore-to-Boston generalization and both long-tail evaluation categories remain. Navsim is mentioned only as a possible source of richer rewards.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated CQL and PPO-lite comparators in Appendix F/Table 11. Its nuScenes Table 1 removes VAD-Tiny, SparseDrive, UAD and World4Drive; VAD matches the retained VAD-Base results. The Navsim comparison is also removed. These substantially change comparator coverage.

E3.justification: Appendix E.3 replaces baseline-selected long-tail subsets with unions of failures from both methods. The L2 subset grows from 984 to 2247 scenes, its 2-second threshold changes from 0.5 to 0.6 m, and the collision subset grows from 91 to 124 scenes. v2 also introduces the L2·Col metric, temporal-augmentation configurations and distinct CQL/PPO-lite evaluation settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds critic-value and policy-divergence diagnostics with and without competition (Figures 5–6), behavior-cloning-weight sensitivity (Table 6), and controls for IL-only inverse masking and mismatched actor masks (Table 3). Long-tail robustness analyses are revised. The existing qualitative cases are retained or relocated, rather than newly added.

E5.justification: v1 Table 1 explicitly identifies random seed 0 for SSR and reports its instability. v2 retains the SSR scores but removes this seed disclosure. Neither version provides repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds temporal CoIRL-AD results averaging 0.45 m L2 and 0.17% collisions, new RL comparisons and sensitivity results. UniAD's Table 1 averages change from 0.69 m/0.12% to 1.03 m/0.31%. Ablation entries change, and Navsim and SSR+CoIRL-AD results disappear. Reconstructed long-tail results replace evaluations under different conditions. The retained LAW+CoIRL-AD main results remain 0.63 m/0.18%; cross-city scores differ only by rounding.

T1.justification: The mathematical substance of the policy, reward, advantage and loss formulations is retained. Tensor dimensions and index corrections clarify existing expressions; neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and v2 adds no substantive derivation or formal assumption.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains competitive dual-policy IL/RL for offline driving. v2 removes the abstract's specific 18% collision-reduction claim, emphasizes expert-anchored robustness, and narrows the introduction/conclusion's empirical support from nuScenes and Navsim to nuScenes. The underlying contribution is retained.

C2.justification: v1 explains unsuccessful RL integration through simple rewards, basic optimization and simulation bias. v2 develops a substantially fuller explanation involving expert-trained world-model errors, value overestimation and competition anchoring exploration. It adds interpretations of mask alignment, behavior-cloning regularization, discounting and optimizer robustness. The qualitative failure cases themselves remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies key settings: competition interval 100, thresholds 1 and 10, interpolation 0.5, discount 0.5 and world-model loss weight 0.2. It also discloses the 1.5-second future-state target and 24-epoch budget, and compares LAW's 10-hour training with CoIRL-AD's previously reported 20 hours. Navsim implementation details are removed; the code-access statement remains.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning around two-stage versus joint IL/RL, adding BC-SAC, Urban Driver, In-RIL and related LLM/LMM training research. RAD is described as IL pretraining followed by RL fine-tuning rather than mixed training. Several references supporting Navsim and generated-data motivation disappear. Publication and title updates to retained works do not themselves count as additions.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and analysis are extensively rewritten. Benchmark and implementation descriptions move into appendices, the appendix hierarchy expands from A.1–A.4 to A–H, and analysis gains separate competition and qualitative subsections. An impact statement and updated affiliation information are also added.

P2.justification: The main paper adopts a two-column layout. Table 1 is reorganized into method categories, multiple tables gain a combined-metric column, and new diagnostic plots and tables appear. The competition flowchart is removed, cross-city/long-tail plots are separated and redrawn as bars, and two existing qualitative figures move into the main text.

improvement.justification: v2 improves long-tail evaluation fairness, supplies important missing hyperparameters and adds useful controls. However, it removes Navsim and SSR-based transfer evidence and drops UAD and SparseDrive, which had lower reported collision rates in v1, while asserting stronger comparative performance. Gains in rigor and reproducibility coexist with materially reduced comparison breadth and completeness, leaving the net quality change uncertain.
